issues.reason: Time states "Rule premises bind through plain variables -- a premise never contains a Skolem term", so (Member (sk_hunt $x) hunt) / (Agent (sk_hunt $x) $x) / (Ongoing (sk_hunt $x)) in the antecedent build a rule that can never fire.

Names and casing fixes that "a participle used as a modifier is an adjective, not the verb" ("a laminated worktop" -> laminated), and Status predicates allows Ongoing only on four explicit markers, none of which a prenominal participle is -- so the restriction is the premise conjunct (Member $x hunting), exactly as the parse itself treated "ground feathers".

Intervals names the licensed head for a non-place "in" -- "an event 'in July' is Time, 'in the final round' the preposition-named In, 'in a statement' likewise In" -- so a document/medium takes (In <event> <log>); (Location sk_write_N sk_log_1) instead asserts the writing event was positioned inside the log, which the sentence does not state.

new_gaps: whether a definite plural's GroupOf typing projects out of an attitude seal is undetermined: the "What projects out of a seal" table names only Member / Name typing of definite and named referents, so the parse's top-level (GroupOf sk_cliffspires_1 cliff_spire) for "the cliff-spires" is unruled either way
an ordinal-day fictional calendar ("on day 396 of Year 2"): (Day <n>) is a day-of-month slot and (Year <n>) a calendar year, so a day-of-year 396 in "Year 2" has no defined reading

a meal-name temporal adjunct ("at breakfast") has no listed Time filler -- the day-part constants are morning / afternoon / evening / night / dawn / noon / dusk, and a meal is neither a day-part nor a calendar term
